finding.title: The `snprintf` function is used to format the HTTP request, but it does not check if the formatted string fits within the buffer size.
The code does not handle errors properly, such as when `send_request` fails or when `recv` fails.
The code does not validate the input arguments, such as the URL and port number.
The code uses a mutex to protect access to the wordlist file, but it does not handle the case where the wordlist file is exhausted.
The `atoi` function is used to convert the port number from a string to an integer. This function does not handle errors, such as invalid input.

findings.description: The `snprintf` function is used to format the HTTP request, but it does not check if the formatted string fits within the buffer size.
The code does not handle errors properly, such as when `send_request` fails or when `recv` fails.
The code does not validate the input arguments, such as the URL and port number.
The code uses a mutex to protect access to the wordlist file, but it does not handle the case where the wordlist file is exhausted.
The `atoi` function is used to convert the port number from a string to an integer. This function does not handle errors, such as invalid input.
